HISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS
35-year-old Qatari man, lives in Zone 74, Al Khor. The episode occurred in March after prolonged outdoor work as nurse for Gulf Care Clinics. Breathlessness, cough, and diffuse wheeze developed after several hours outdoors, accompanied by headache, weakness, and nausea. Skin is warm and dry, but mental status is normal and there is no neck stiffness. Temperature is 38.3°C, pulse 122/min, blood pressure 108/64 mmHg, respiratory rate 32/min, and oxygen saturation 90% on room air. Serum sodium is 138 mmol/L, creatinine 78 µmol/L, lactate 1.8 mmol/L, and glucose 6.1 mmol/L. Chest radiography is clear. After cooling, intravenous fluids, and inhaled bronchodilators, temperature falls and respiratory distress improves substantially.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
nil significant

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Working diagnosis withheld for review. Admit / treat per protocol; senior review requested.
Attending: Dr. Hessa Al-Marri
L0.findings: Prolonged outdoor heat exposure followed by hyperthermia, tachycardia, tachypnea, headache, weakness, nausea, warm dry skin, and improvement with cooling and fluids strongly supports heat stroke; diffuse wheeze and bronchodilator response support concurrent asthma exacerbation, while fever and physiological stress make sepsis a less likely alternative.

High-sensitivity troponin-I is 73 ng/L initially and 520 ng/L after two hours; creatinine is 87 µmol/L, potassium is 4.3 mmol/L, and hemoglobin is 14.5 g/dL.

segments.text: Severe abdominal pain, nausea, and weakness developed after prolonged outdoor activity. Serum sodium is 136 mmol/L, creatinine 118 µmol/L, lactate 2.8 mmol/L, and white-cell count 16.2 ×10⁹/L with neutrophilia. After cooling and intravenous fluids, temperature and blood pressure improve, but focal abdominal pain persists. CT shows periappendiceal inflammation without perforation.
